disease_label_per_paper: Nocardia farcinica brain abscess in an immunocompetent patient
presentation_summary: 71-year-old man with hypertension presented with headache, dizziness, and nausea for three days.
Initial vital signs were blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 76/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and temperature 36.9 C; he was alert.
Physical, cardiopulmonary, abdominal, and neurologic examinations were normal, with no fever, neck stiffness, photophobia, or papilledema.

Initial labs showed WBC 11.2 x10^9/L, neutrophils 64.6%, hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL, platelets 211 x10^9/L, ESR 38 mm/hr, CRP 1.11 mg/dL, creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, sodium 136 mEq/L, and negative HIV/HBV/HCV serology.
Chest and abdomen radiographs were normal; brain CT and MRI showed multiple rim-enhancing lesions with surrounding edema, including a right occipital abscess.
He underwent stereotactic aspiration; pus later grew Nocardia farcinica by culture and 16S rRNA sequencing, and repeat surgery was needed on hospital day 24 because abscess and edema increased.
After repeated surgery and susceptibility-directed combination antibiotics, he improved, was discharged on hospital day 67, and follow-up CT showed resolution.

quality_warnings: Nocardia culture, AFB stain, 16S sequencing, and susceptibility are post-aspiration confirmatory evidence with use_in_ranking=false.
Repeat surgery and radiographic resolution are course evidence only, not presentation ranking evidence.
Normal neurologic exam and absent fever/meningeal signs are retained as negative presentation evidence rather than omitted.
